title: Affine higher direct images lower the transcendence-degree support bound
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be schemes of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine $K$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. For each integer $b$, put $E_b(T)=\{t\in T:\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(t)\leq b\}$, with $E_b(T)=\varnothing$ for $b<0$, using [def-kun-support] and [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Let $a\geq0$ be an integer and $F$ a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] whose support is contained in $E_a(X)$. Then, for every $q\geq0$, the support of $R^qf_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is contained in $E_{a-q}(Y)$.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point outside E_(a-q)(Y). Use lem-kun-finite-type-residue-trdeg to write its residue transcendence degree as a natural number b; the complement condition and a >= 0 give a.toNat < b+q, including q=0 and q>a. Choose the compatible affine models over a separably closed field L supplied by lem-kun-strict-local-algebraic-residue-models, with trdeg_K L=b.

Regard the model diagram over Y by composing its morphisms to U with the open immersion U -> Y. This preserves its cofiltered limit: the forgetful functors from over categories preserve and reflect connected limits. Apply Over.pullback f, a right adjoint, and then forget to schemes. The resulting cone is a limit of T_i=V_i x_Y X. The T_i and their transitions are affine by lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence. The morphism f is locally of finite type since its composite to Spec K is; base change and composition make T_i finite type over L. The given cone vertex identification and the pullback universal property identify the limit with X x_Y Y_(s), respecting its projection to X.

For z in T_i, the map on residue fields of V_i -> U is algebraic by the model theorem; composing with U -> Y preserves this because open immersions induce residue-field isomorphisms. Apply lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field. The tensor product of kappa(z_X) and the algebraic extension kappa(z_V) over kappa(y) is integral over kappa(z_X), by stability of integrality under base change. Its prime quotient is an integral domain integral over a field, hence a field. The compatible residue-field isomorphism identifies kappa(z) with this quotient, proving algebraicity over kappa(z_X). The inverse-image stalk comparison gives support(p_i^* F) subset p_i^-1(support F). Torsion pulls back by its stalk characterization.

On the pulled-back support the two compatible field towers give b+trdeg_L kappa(z)=trdeg_K kappa(z_X)<=a.toNat, using lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower and algebraicity from the preceding step. If b<=a.toNat, cancel the finite cardinal b to get support bound a.toNat-b. Apply lem-kun-affine-support-vanishing, since q>a.toNat-b. If b>a.toNat the support is empty, so the geometric-stalk conservative family makes the sheaf zero, and its cohomology is zero. Use lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison to express both conclusions in Sheaf.H.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-etale-cohomology-cocone to the pulled-back model diagram and its natural transformation to X. Every stage cohomology group is zero; hence the entire diagram is zero and its colimit is zero. Its comparison isomorphism gives zero cohomology on the limit. Transport across the vertex isomorphism by cohomology invariance under scheme isomorphisms, the isomorphism case of prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos, and inverse-image composition. Convert Sheaf.H to derived global sections by lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison. Finally prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula identifies this zero group with the chosen geometric stalk. Unfolding def-kun-support proves the asserted containment.
